The game is played on a chess board sized 8x8 starting with 4 black checkers (the wolves) on one side and a single white checker (the sheep) on the other side. The wolves hunt the sheep. The sheep moves diagonally one field range forward or backward onto an empty adjacent square per turn. Wolves can only move diagonally one field forward onto an empty adjacent square. There is no capturing by jumping and no stacking of checkers. Sheep wins by reaching the other side of the board. Wolves win by blocking the sheep such that it cannot move anymore. A simple game to teach children (as it is actually done in schools). Number of players: 2 Game duration: 3 mn Complexity: 1 / 5 Play Wolf and Sheep and 1414 other games online. WHITE : Sheep needs to pass through the wolves and reach their starting line. Components A Chess like board 1 white token (called "Sheep") 4 black tokens (called "Wolves") Setup Wolves are placed onto fields B8, D8, F8, and H8. Sheep starts the game from E1. Start of the game On Your Turn You can move : 1 piece at a time only diagonally (so you always play on the same cell color of the board) only 1 step at a time the sheep can move backward, not the wolves End of game Beware this is an asymmetric game : WHITE Victory : Sheep wins by reaching the other side of the board (8th row or 10th row according to played variant). WHITE BGA auto victory : if there is not enough wolves in front of the sheep to block the sheep. BLACK Victory : Wolves win by blocking the sheep such that it cannot move anymore (when sheep has no legal move left). Variants Board size Chess board : 8x8 Checkers board : 10x10 (+1 black token) Duration 1 round is a classic play as defined here 2 rounds : One round with Player 1 as White VS Player 2 as Black, then one round with Player 2 as White VS Player 1 as Black User Preferences Board colors Tokens on dark cells : Tokens are places as in the pictures on the "black"/darkest cells of the board Tokens on light cells : Tokens are places on the "white"/brightest cells of the board Interface theme Standard : the same background as any classic BGA game like Chess. [Rating: 3/10] Solved game but also incredibly easy to solve compared to other, similar abstract games. Also... not very interesting. The one good thing I would say is that at least it is quick.

[Rating: 4/10] Like Tic-Tac-Toe or Nim, this is a game of learning the singular solvable strategy. However, since the sides are asymmetrical, having an adult play the fox while a child plays the hounds can be an interesting exercise and develop some tactical thinking skills. I find this game preferable to either of the others mentioned for that reason. It can also serve as a good introduction to the way pieces move in Checkers without all the board complexity right off the bat (though there is no jumping either).
